title: Is the Winspace G3 the Best Value Gravel Bike?

takeaways.text: After about four weeks on a bike lent by UK dealer Wood Cycles, the reviewer called it one of the most impressive frames he had ridden: quick to accelerate and lively, while the position stayed slightly upright and comfortable from the first ride.
UDH, a 68 mm T47 shell that is easy to service without touching paint, and internal routing that still gave clean GRX mechanical shifting.
Ridden on 50 mm Cinturato-type gravel tires, matching Winspace's 50 mm claim; he kept pace on group road rides and climbs without swapping to slicks.

Compared on geometry with Winspace's M6 road frame: slightly shorter reach, about 37 mm more stack at the equivalent size, more sloping top tube, higher bottom bracket and longer wheelbase, so it is a little less nimble in tight road bends.
Quoted as £1,250 for the frameset in mid-2026.

disclosure: The reviewer says Woods Cycles, a retailer that sells Winspace, gave him access to the bike for the review.
summary: Review after about four weeks on a G3 with mechanical GRX, ridden on a mixed road and gravel loop, covering ride feel, internal routing, frame price and upgrade paths.
